definitions.gloss: true feelings; real intention; what one really thinks
definitions.explanation: One's genuine thoughts or feelings as opposed to what one expresses publicly for social harmony.

examples.japanese: {本音|ほんね}を{言|い}うと、あまり{行|い}きたくない。
examples.english: To tell you the truth, I don't really want to go.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{本音|ほんね}がやっと{分|わ}かった。
examples.english: I finally understood his true feelings.

examples.japanese: お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}むと{本音|ほんね}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: When people drink alcohol, their true feelings come out.

notes:
CULTURAL CONCEPT:
{本音|ほんね} and {建前|たてまえ} are a fundamental pair in understanding Japanese communication. {本音|ほんね} represents one's genuine, private thoughts while {建前|たてまえ} is the public stance maintained for social harmony.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{本音|ほんね}を{言|い}う / {本音|ほんね}を{吐|は}く (to speak one's true feelings)
・{本音|ほんね}が{出|で}る (one's true feelings come out)
・{本音|ほんね}を{隠|かく}す (to hide one's true feelings)
・{本音|ほんね}と{建前|たてまえ} (true feelings and public stance)

USAGE NOTE:
Often used when revealing something that contrasts with what was previously expressed or expected.
